meta.title: Who really said "Never say never, because limits, like fears, are often just an illusion"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Michael Jordan, closing his Basketball Hall of Fame speech on 11 September 2009 — right after joking he might still be playing at 50. It is the last thing he says.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Never say never, because limits, like fears, are often just an illusion'?
meta.ogDescription: Michael Jordan — the closing words of his Basketball Hall of Fame enshrinement speech, 11 September 2009, following a joke about playing at 50.

answer.label: Spoken by
answer.authorDates: b. 1963 · American basketball player, Chicago Bulls & Washington Wizards
answer.sourceLine: These are the closing words of Jordan’s Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame enshrinement speech, delivered in Springfield, Massachusetts on 11 September 2009. They are not free-floating motivation: he had just said he did not see the honour as an ending, joked that “one day you might look up and see me playing the game at 50”, and answered the laughter with “Oh don’t laugh. Never say never. Because limits, like fears are often just an illusion.” The circulating version joins those two sentences with a comma; the words themselves are unchanged.

source.heading: The closing of the speech

docMeta.dd: Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame enshrinement, Class of 2009
The final lines, immediately before “Thank you very much”

source.excerpt: Although I’m recognized with this tremendous honor of being in the basketball Hall of Fame — I don’t look at this moment as a defining end to my relationship with the game of basketball. It’s simply a continuation of something that I started a long time ago. One day you might look up and see me playing the game at 50. (laughs) Oh don’t laugh. Never say never. Because limits, like fears are often just an illusion. Thank you very much.
trail: Speakola publishes the speech in full ↗, datelined 11 September 2009, Springfield, MA. Its closing runs: “One day you might look up and see me playing the game at 50. (laughs) Oh don’t laugh. Never say never. Because limits, like fears are often just an illusion. Thank you very much.” That is the whole of the quotation, in order, with the joke it answers.

Wikiquote lists “Limits, like fears, are often just an illusion” ↗ and sources it to the 2009 Hall of Fame induction address — an independent attribution of the line to the same speech. Wikiquote records only that clause, not the “Never say never” sentence before it, which is why the fuller passage above matters.

Wikipedia confirms the occasion ↗: Jordan was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2009 for his individual career (and again in 2010 with the 1992 Dream Team), and it describes the September 2009 induction speech, including that David Thompson presented him.

A second Wikipedia article fixes the date independently ↗, recording that the Associated Press photograph behind the “Crying Jordan” meme was taken by Stephan Savoia during this induction ceremony on September 11, 2009 — the same day Speakola gives.
source.excerptNote: Transcribed from the speech as published by Speakola, which dates it 11 September 2009, Springfield, MA. Note the punctuation: the transcript sets “Never say never.” as its own sentence, with “Because limits…” beginning the next and no comma after “fears”. Punctuating speech is a transcriber’s decision, so renderings differ; the words and their order do not.

source.rightsNote: A speech delivered in 2009 is comfortably inside copyright in the United States; nothing about a quotation being widely repeated online changes that. The words are Jordan’s own rather than work-for-hire, so the rights in the text sit with him, while the broadcast recording of the ceremony carries its own separate rights. The passage is reproduced here briefly for identification and commentary.

author.name: Michael Jordan
author.heading: About Michael Jordan
author.bio: Michael Jordan played fifteen seasons in the NBA for the Chicago Bulls and Washington Wizards and is widely considered the greatest basketball player of all time. He retired three times, which is the joke behind this quotation: by 2009 an audience had every reason to laugh at him hinting he might play again. He entered the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame twice — in 2009 for his individual career, and in 2010 as part of the 1992 Olympic “Dream Team”.

misattribution.heading: How it travels
misattribution.intro: The attribution is not in dispute — this is Jordan’s line, from a documented speech. What the internet drops is the punctuation and the joke, which is worth noting because the line reads as generic motivation once it is cut loose from the moment that produced it.

items.who: “Never say never, because limits, like fears, are often just an illusion.”
items.why: The transcript sets these as two sentences ↗ and omits the comma after “fears”. No word is added, removed or reordered, so this is a rendering choice rather than a misquotation.

items.who: “One day you might look up and see me playing the game at 50. (laughs) Oh don’t laugh.”
items.why: Quoted alone, the line sounds like a maxim about ambition. In the speech it is a punchline ↗ — Jordan is defending a joke about still playing basketball in his fifties.

misattribution.truthLine: Correctly attributed, correctly worded. The only thing usually lost is that it is the last thing he said, and that he was answering laughter ↗.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Jordan’s 2009 enshrinement speech is remembered less for grace than for grievance: he used it to work through decades of slights, real and collected, and the Associated Press photograph of him in tears during it became the “Crying Jordan” meme. The closing lines are the turn at the end of that — the point where the accounting stops and he refuses to treat the honour as a full stop.

That is what the quotation is actually doing. He had already said he did not see the Hall of Fame as “a defining end to my relationship with the game”, then floated the idea of playing at 50. The room laughed. “Never say never” is him not accepting the laugh.
context.pull: It is not a maxim about ambition. It is a man refusing to let a room laugh him into retirement.
